b: I've been struggling with a very strange sleep problem for years, and I'm honestly desperate to find someone who has experienced something similar.

When I first fall asleep at night, I feel like I never enter deep sleep. I stay in this very light, almost conscious state of sleep, where I feel aware of everything around me. I can spend the entire night like this and wake up completely exhausted, feeling like I just closed my eyes all night instead of actually sleeping.
The weirdest part is that I CAN sometimes get deep, restorative sleep, but only after waking up and falling asleep again, usually multiple times.

It's almost like my brain needs several sleep/wake cycles before it finally switches into proper sleep. Sometimes I have to wake up two, three, or even more times before I finally experience what feels like real deep sleep. This often happens toward the morning.

I've had sleep studies done, and I was diagnosed with mild sleep apnea (around 8 hypopneas per hour). I've tried both a mandibular advancement device and CPAP, but neither has solved this specific problem.
Even with treatment, I still have to go through this strange process of falling asleep, waking up, and falling asleep again before I can finally get restorative sleep.

Has anyone experienced this exact pattern, where your first period of sleep is always light and unrefreshing, but sleep after several awakenings feels much deeper?Did you ever figure out what was causing it?
I'm so exhausted from never feeling rested. It's affecting my entire life, and I feel like I'm going crazy trying to understand what's wrong.
I'd really appreciate hearing from anyone who has experienced something similar, especially if you found an explanation or a solution.
